messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details: The failing test `isUnixSymlinkIsFalseIfMoreThanOneFlagIsSet` asserts that `isUnixSymlink()` should return false for a zip entry "META-INF/maven/". According to the test, the `ZipArchiveEntry` for this path should not be recognized as a Unix symlink if more than one Unix permission flag is set on that entry.

The method `ZipArchiveEntry.isUnixSymlink()` returns true if and only if the Unix mode of the entry, masked by the constant `UnixStat.LINK_FLAG` (which is octal 0120000, representing the symlink file type bit), exactly matches the symlink flag.

`ZipArchiveEntry.getUnixMode()` returns the Unix mode extracted from the external attributes field if the entry platform is Unix, otherwise zero. This mode is obtained by right-shifting and masking the external attributes.

The current bug report describes a scenario where the Unix permission bits set on the entry are `177777` (octal), which means more bits beyond just the symlink flag are set on the entry. This causes `isUnixSymlink()` to return true even though the entry is not strictly just a symlink file type — it has other bits set that mark it as invalid or a different type.

The problem arises because the `isUnixSymlink()` method checks for an exact match to the symlink flag bits but does so by a strict equality:

```java
(getUnixMode() & UnixStat.LINK_FLAG) == UnixStat.LINK_FLAG
```

This condition returns true even if extra bits outside LINK_FLAG are set, as long as the LINK_FLAG bit is present. If the mode is `177777`, the bitwise AND with `LINK_FLAG` will still yield `LINK_FLAG`, so the method wrongly returns true.

Therefore, the method does not sufficiently verify that the Unix mode has only the link flag set as its file type. It should also check that no other file type bits are set to avoid false positives for corrupted or invalid entries.

In conclusion, the root cause of the failure is an overly permissive check in `ZipArchiveEntry.isUnixSymlink()` that returns true if the symlink bit is set anywhere in the mode rather than confirming that the mode solely indicates a symlink.

The other recent bug reports are unrelated to this specific logic. The code review and current bug report align, showing that the issue is with the logic in `isUnixSymlink()` in handling external attributes and Unix mode flags.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
